summary: Tenant hotspot causing ephemeral GPU depletion and rollover delays in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusAI reported a sharp degradation in throughput for their reserved dedicated pool during a 30-minute window on 2026-03-10. The pool hit ephemeral GPU depletion and automatic rollover to fallback variants was delayed, leading to elevated p95/p99 latency and 429s for the customer.

Impact:
- NimbusAI experienced 20-40% reduced throughput across pinned routes and a 5x increase in p99 latency for short-stream requests.
- Multiple customer endpoints returned 429 (throttled) and some short streams saw connection resets.
- Impacted a single dedicated pool in us-west-2; other customers on the same pool saw transient requests slowdown but not complete outages.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool "dp-usw2-42" (production), mixed GPU types (A100, H100), autoscaler enabled, default cooldowns.
- Customer pinned redwood-open-7B for route /generate-chat; some traffic uses redwood-3b-v2 for embeddings.

Steps to reproduce (observed in telemetry):
1) Customer deploys a small real-time agent that rapidly reconnects and loads model context per request (many short-lived sessions).
2) Within a 5m window traffic pattern shifts to 10k short streams/min with high session churn.
3) Allocator begins to fragment slot leases; autoscaler triggers a scale-up but allocation attach latency increases.
4) GPUs appear provisioned but are temporarily unusable due to slot fragmentation/lease contention and kv-prefetch thrashing.

Observed behavior:
- p95 latency climbs from ~80ms to 300-600ms; p99 spikes to multiple seconds.
- Autoscaler scales up but new nodes remain underutilized while attach retries increase.
- Logs show many "lease_acquire_timeout" and "slot_in_use" entries plus prefetch eviction warnings.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should add capacity and allocator should attach new GPUs within SLO; short sessions should not cause pool-wide fragmentation.

Initial logs & links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dp-usw2-42/throughput?orgId=1 (p95/p99 graphs attached in runbook)
- Recent sidecar logs: "lease_acquire_timeout: 00:00:02" repeated ~12k times in 20m
- Console traces show increased attach latency around 2026-03-10T15:12:00Z

Initial triage summary:
Support confirmed pattern is a noisy-tenant hotspot: high short-stream fanout and rapid reconnects caused allocator and prefetch subsystems to thrash. Autoscaler responded but attach/lease contention prevented bandwidth from being realized, causing the customer-visible throughput drop. Temporary mitigation and longer-term fixes are required.
comments: 2026-03-10T12:40:00Z - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged, collecting logs and requested sample request IDs and customer traffic pattern. Asked NimbusAI for a recent curl trace and SDK call timestamps.

2026-03-10T13:05:00Z - Customer (NimbusAI - Martin Liu): Provided SDK logs showing rapid session open/close every 200ms for many shards; attached request-id headers. Noted that agent reconnects are intentional for quick cold-start isolation.

2026-03-10T13:20:00Z - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed surge in lease_acquire_timeout and prefetch eviction metrics. Marking potential allocator fragmentation + kv-cache pressure. Spun up additional debug logs on allocator and set temporary autoscaler override to hold new nodes in warm state for 10m.

2026-03-10T14:00:00Z - Support (Aisha Patel): Applied short-term mitigation: applied a tenant-specific soft-rate limit (reduce max simultaneous short streams from 800 to 150) and enabled per-tenant connection pooling. Customer confirmed immediate improvement in new requests.

2026-03-10T16:45:00Z - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Noted that after mitigation, attach latency dropped back toward baseline and 429s decreased. We'll keep autoscaler override for 24h while engineering implements allocator fixes.
2026-03-11T09:10:00Z - Product (Sofia Martinez): Raised follow-up to product: consider exposing per-tenant session churn controls in Console and recommend SDK pooling defaults in docs.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Noisy-tenant short-stream fanout causes allocator lease fragmentation and repeated prefetch eviction, preventing newly scaled GPUs from being used immediately.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler cooldown and our slot compaction window are too aggressive for rapid transient spikes; scale-up occurs but allocator remains stuck on busy slots, so capacity is not realized.
Telemetry evidence: lease_acquire_timeout count correlates with p99 spike window (Pearson r=.87). Prefetch cache eviction rate increased by 6x during the event.
Checked driver/host metrics: no GPU thermal throttling, PCIe errors, or OOMs recorded. Suggests logical contention rather than hardware failure.
Reproduced locally on staging with simulated churn: spinning up 5k short streams/min caused slot fragmentation and attach retry storms. Re-running with connection pooling eliminated the problem.

Potential root cause: tenant's connection pattern plus small-session allocation granularity leads to heavy slot churn; allocator lacks immediate compaction and leases are held for short durations leading to effective capacity loss.

Related historical tickets: SUP-77109 (autoscale miss-batch-saturation) and SUP-903210 (interleaved-affinity mismatch). Some common signals but different manifestation (this one is short-session churn driven).
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-10):
- Tenant soft-rate limit on short streams (applied via per-tenant policy).
- Enabled SDK connection pooling recommendation to customer and rolled out per-tenant connection pooling on gateway for NimbusAI.
- Temporarily increased autoscaler warm-hold period from 2m to 10m for the affected pool to avoid immediate shrink/rebalance.
Customer reported throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline within 30 minutes after mitigations were applied. 429s and p99 spikes subsided.

Medium-term engineering fixes (in-progress):
- PR #1287 for allocator: lease compaction algorithm to reduce fragmentation and a background slot consolidation worker. (See related PR link).
- Autoscaler change: add churn-detection signal to delay shrink and to prefer slot compaction before failing attach.
- Console change: Add per-tenant "session-churn" alert and a guided remediation (rate-limit / pool warm-hold toggle).

Long-term recommendations for customers:
- Prefer SDK connection pooling for high-frequency short requests.
- Use persistent sessions when possible to reduce allocation churn.
- For heavy short-stream workloads, consider a dedicated smaller pool with longer warm-hold settings.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering to validate allocator compaction in staging with churn test by 2026-03-18.
- Product to spec Console controls for per-tenant churn protection by 2026-04-01.
- Support to reach back out to NimbusAI with postmortem and SDK guidance once fixes land.
